sentences.text: Priya Nair, from adult social care, met with Margaret Doyle, and Kevin Doyle, Margaret's son, for a needs assessment, which was referred by the hospital after Margaret was discharged (Ln 1, Ln 21, Ln 23, Ln 24).
The purpose of the visit was to conduct a needs assessment under the Care Act to understand how Margaret is managing day to day, what is difficult, what is working, and what matters to her (Ln 26).
Margaret expressed that she did not want to be put anywhere, and Priya confirmed that the assessment was about helping her stay in her home (Ln 29, Ln 30, Ln 31).
Margaret suffered a fall on the third of March while in the kitchen, where she was going to make tea (Ln 52, Ln 54, Ln 55, Ln 56).
After the fall, Margaret could not get up, and she landed on her wrist, which she could not put any weight on (Ln 58, Ln 59).
She was on the floor for about two hours until Brenda next door found her (Ln 61, Ln 63).
Margaret fractured her left wrist, which is her good hand as she is left-handed, making tasks like opening jars and doing buttons difficult (Ln 83, Ln 84, Ln 86).
She uses a frame indoors, which she dislikes, but she uses it mostly, although sometimes she holds onto furniture instead because the frame gets caught on rugs or doorframes (Ln 97, Ln 100, Ln 102).
Outdoors, she uses Frank's old stick, but she has only been out to the end of the path, except for one trip to the doctor's with Kevin (Ln 104, Ln 105).
She stated that before the fall, she could walk to the shops (about ten minutes), but now she is frightened of going out again (Ln 107, Ln 110).

Margaret has experienced three falls in the last six months, including the one in March, one before Christmas in the garden, and one in January in the bathroom where she caught herself on the sink (Ln 116, Ln 117, Ln 115).

She has to use the stairs to get to the upstairs bedroom and toilet, and she goes up one at a time using her right hand on the rail, but coming down is worse as the rail is on the wrong side, sometimes causing her to go down on her bottom (Ln 133, Ln 140, Ln 141, Ln 143).

She currently manages washing with a strip wash at the upstairs sink, but she has not had a proper bath since before the January fall because she fears getting out and not being found if she gets stuck (Ln 181, Ln 183, Ln 184, Ln 187).
Margaret stated that she wants to stay in her own home, as it is where she brought up her children, and she knows every creak in the house (Ln 344, Ln 346, Ln 347).
Margaret stated that what matters to her is being able to have a proper bath and wash her hair (Ln 196, Ln 594).
She wishes to get back to the lunch club, seeing Joan and Pat (Ln 595).
Margaret wishes to be able to cook proper dinners again, not every day, but now and then (Ln 598).
She wants to be able to see Frank's roses come out this summer (Ln 601, Ln 602).
Margaret stated that she wants to stay in her own home for as long as she possibly can (Ln 347).
Margaret admitted to missing her blood pressure tablet twice last week, which she attributed to being 'all over the place' since the fall (Ln 293, Ln 296).
Margaret admitted to sometimes not getting dressed, stating that some days she thought 'what's the point, nobody's coming' (Ln 213).
Margaret reported sometimes not making it to the toilet if she leaves it too long, leading to some leaking, and she wears pads at night (Ln 220, Ln 221, Ln 223).

Margaret disclosed that her grandson, Jordan, has been borrowing her bank card and that about six hundred pounds has been withdrawn over the last two months, which she did not ask him to take (Ln 471, Ln 475, Ln 478, Ln 520, Ln 521).
Kevin reported that Brenda mentioned to him that she thought she saw Jordan at the cash machine on the high street with a card, though she was not sure it was him (Ln 526, Ln 527, Ln 530).
Kevin also mentioned that he heard from one of Jordan's old mates' mums that Jordan might have gotten into debt with betting on his phone (Ln 531).
Priya stated that she has a duty to take the information about the money being taken seriously as a safeguarding concern (Ln 544).
Kevin Doyle, Margaret's son, visits mainly on Sundays, where he does the big shop, and sometimes midweek if he is on early shifts (Ln 366, Ln 367).
Margaret's daughter, Susan, lives in Spain and rings every Sunday night, and she visits in the summer (Ln 372, Ln 374).
Brenda, a neighbour, pops in most days, sometimes just for a minute, and they have a routine of knocking on the wall in the morning to check on each other (Ln 379, Ln 380).
Margaret used to attend a lunch club at St Michael's church hall every Wednesday, but she has not been since the fall (Ln 385, Ln 392).
Margaret receives her state pension and half of Frank's widow's pension (Ln 570).
She has approximately nine thousand pounds in the building society, which she states is her funeral money and some for the grandchildren (Ln 574).
Margaret mentioned that she is not sure where her money has been going, stating she has been 'a bit short lately' (Ln 308, Ln 309).

Priya will make a referral to occupational therapy today for Margaret to look at a bath lift/board, a second rail on the stairs, a second frame for upstairs, and the back step/pull cord light (Ln 626, Ln 627).
Priya will make a safeguarding referral about the card this afternoon (Ln 630).
Priya will refer Margaret for the telecare alarm/watch that can detect a fall, which usually takes about ten days to fit (Ln 632, Ln 633).

Priya will write to Dr Shah regarding a referral to the falls clinic, mentioning weight loss, continence service, and missed tablets, and will also contact the chemist about an easier-to-open medication pack (Ln 635, Ln 636).
Priya will put in a request for reablement visits (morning and teatime) and will inform Margaret of the outcome by the end of next week (Ln 639).
Priya will find out about transport options for Margaret to attend the lunch club at St Michael's on Thursdays (Ln 640).
Kevin will take Margaret to the Midshire building society branch on Friday morning to cancel the card and order a new one (Ln 559, Ln 624, Ln 643).
Kevin will help Margaret with the Attendance Allowance form, which Priya will post out, and they plan to do this on Sunday (Ln 645, Ln 646).
Priya will call Margaret on Monday to check in after the building society visit (Ln 653).
Priya plans to see Margaret again on Tuesday the fifteenth of April at two o'clock (Ln 656).
